results.name: Kerma Culture Burial (~2050-1750 BC)
results.description:
Scanned at the British Museum from behind a glass display case.

Plaque Reads:

"This reconstructed burial shows a typical Kerma culture grave from a cemetery in northern Sudan. The man has been placed in a crouched position on his right side, his head to the east, facing north. Sacrificed sheep/goats are by his feet, with pottery vessels and joints of meat to one side. Such ritual practices suggest that these people believed in some form of afterlife. Analysis of the skeleton showed that these are the remains of an adult male who was ~1.75m tall. He died between the ages of 35 & 50 & his teeth are heavily worn. This has led to dental disease and his upper jaw (maxilla) has a large abscess above one of the incisors. The healed fractures on his feet, ribs and long bones suggest an active or violent life. The fracture on his right ulna -called a parry fracture - usually occurs when the arm is lifted to deflect a blow to the head. The meat offerings from the sheep &/or goats, are all from young animals"

results.name: Tool for lifting Displays (NHMW-AFW-DING-0093)
results.description:
3D scans of a tool for lifting the heavy glass doors/sides of the large historical display cases in the Natural History Museum. The tool was used during the late 19th century, later display cases had hinged doors and didn’t require a lifting device.

The tool is not on display and can be viewed by appointment.

**Inventory number:** NHMW-AFW-DING-0093

**Collection:** Natural History Museum Vienna, Archive for the History of Science, 3D Objects/Special Collection

Find out more about the NHM Vienna [here](http://www.nhm-wien.ac.at/en).

Scanned and edited by Pauline Forsthuber and Anna Haider (NHMW)

Scanner: Artec Eva.

This object was digitized with funding from the "Kulturerbe digital" program of the Federal Ministry Republic of Austria for Arts, Culture, Civil Service and Sport.

results.name: Clay figure in display box
results.description:
Figure captured in Mascota Archaelogical Museum in Mascota, Jalisco, Mexico.
Captured through glass display case so no back and lower quality than otherwise possible. I also used a poor choice of focal depth resulting in blurriness in places.

ARCHAEOLOGICAL MUSEUM OF MASCOTA
If you are interested in history and the social sciences, you cannot miss the opportunity of visiting the Archaeological Museum, located in the Town of Mascota, Jalisco. 

The Museum has a total of 600 pieces in the exhibition and some remains date back almost 3000 years ago. Pieces include clay work from the region, offerings of the Olmec and Wixarika cultures, and even some of the Andean region.

results.name: Lead Glass Goblet with 3DF Zephyr (Video)
results.description:
A Lead Glass Goblet, Goblet and Cover, reconstructed in 3DF Zephyr free version, from the V&A museum, for the assessment INST0044: Introduction to Digitisation.

* Shooting environment:The light is hard and dim because it was taken in the museum hall. The goblet is displayed in a glass display case, which posed another challenge for reconstruction due to other reflection.

* Post-produciton: Post-processing adjustments have been made to adjust the white balance, exposure and colour calibration,but the poor quality of the images prevented the most accurate colour management from being achieved.

* Input-data: 50 images were extracted from a 4k video, 26 images successfully oriented.

* Collection information: https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O5248/goblet-and-cover-unknown/
